# Neotoma's incumbent: what Candidate B uses today instead, and where it fails them

## Subject

The reader's current workaround for ad-hoc agent state — not a competing vendor, but a pile of markdown files, a Notion/Airtable database, re-prompting, or a homegrown script over flat files. This is the incumbent the product actually displaces for the durable ICP (Candidate B); the infrastructure-builder's homegrown Postgres/MCP stack (Candidate A) is a validator of the problem, not the primary competitive comparison, per the O1 durable-ICP ruling.

## Summary

Candidate B does not arrive using a competing product. They patch: a growing set of markdown files (CLAUDE.md/SOUL.md-style), a Notion or Airtable database they already suspect is a dead end, raw re-prompting/copy-paste between tools, or platform-native memory (Claude Projects KB, Claude chat memory, ChatGPT memory) that is single-tool and non-portable. Specific failure modes, per incumbent (primary_icp.md competitor-migration table): markdown/flat files do not scale — agents end up writing Python scripts to manage the files, and there is no schema enforcement, so structure decays as it grows. Notion/Airtable is fine for human editing but breaks the moment an agent needs to read and write it — there are insufficient hooks for inter-agent validation, so agents either bypass the structure or corrupt it silently. Platform memory (Claude chat memory, ChatGPT memory) is retrieval-based, not state-based: opaque, non-auditable, single-tool, no schema, no write surface a second tool can share. Raw re-prompting has no persistence at all — the attention tax compounds daily and context is lost every session. The common thread across all four: nothing is ever committed to an authoritative record, so corrections do not stick and there is no single place a fact is settled once. This is corroborated by field evidence: an evaluator's own homepage-feedback session ([evaluator-record]) independently surfaced 'already building own memory system' as the single strongest-resonating homepage block, and the full-corpus evaluator classification (ent_d4d44f0d63a1a5a6d61e3a19) names specific incumbents builders had already assembled before evaluating Neotoma — a ralph-loop+markdown CRM, a 'librarian script' over 100+ markdown files, a custom Postgres MCP, a 150-file split-brain — all instances of the same patching pattern, at the more advanced (Candidate A) end of it.

## Method

Read the product's decision register (plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f) for the settled category and ICP; read the competitor-migration table in neotoma primary_icp.md (internal, market-derived); cross-checked against named evaluator evidence synthesized in feedback ent_d4d44f0d63a1a5a6d61e3a19 (full corpus classification of ~33 engaged evaluators into latent/active demand, mapped 1:1 onto operator-vs-builder) and customer_development_note entities for an evaluator ([evaluator-record]) and an evaluator ([evaluator-record]). Applied the competitor test from plan decision scenarios_must_fail_the_competitor_test (2026-08-21): could mem0, Zep, or another retrieval-memory vendor plausibly claim to solve this failure mode? Failure modes that a retrieval vendor could claim were excluded or reframed.

## Conclusion

What Neotoma resolves, for Candidate B specifically: a single authoritative record any agent or tool can read and write, with versioned observations, field-level provenance, and corrections that hold everywhere once made — the exact failure mode markdown files, Notion, and platform memory share (nothing is ever settled anywhere). What it does NOT resolve, and copy must not claim it does: it does not make the reader's agents smarter, does not do retrieval/RAG-style semantic recall as its primary value (that is an optional secondary capability, not the differentiator), and does not remove the need to run something locally — a guided app installer is intended but not shipped as of 2026-09-15 (decision onboarding_is_guided_app_install), so today's install still runs through npm + CLI. Competitor test applied per scenario: 'your agent forgot' framing was rejected outright — any retrieval-memory vendor answers a recall complaint directly, so copy must say a fact was never committed to a record, not that it was forgotten (decision never_say_the_agent_forgot). The homegrown-Postgres/custom-MCP incumbent (what Candidate A already built) was considered and set aside as the PRIMARY incumbent for Candidate B: that comparison undersells the point, since Candidate B is defined by NOT building that stack (O1). It remains a valid secondary comparison for the Candidate A early-adopter cohort. The attestation/capability-grants surface must not appear anywhere in this comparison as a reason to switch — it is infrastructure serving the product's own guarantees, not a sold feature (decision attestation_surface_is_infrastructure, O3); it may only be cited as evidence supporting the provenance guarantee itself.
